text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.9% today as oil prices weakened and the energy sector faced a broader pullback. U.S. crude dropped to $89.53 per barrel, pulling back from recent highs, while a headline from major financial media noted that "the biggest money-making energy trade looks over" — specifically referring to refinery-related stocks unwinding their gains. For an integrated energy company like this one, lower crude prices directly reduce profit margins and future cash flow from production and operations.

The sell-off also reflects a shift in market sentiment around energy stocks more broadly. The failed climate talks at COP31, where a deal without fossil fuel language was rejected, underscores long-term policy headwinds for oil producers, even as near-term geopolitical tensions in the Middle East (Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries, Iran-backed incidents) have kept energy in focus. With the refinery-driven profit cycle apparently cooling, investors appear to be rotating away from the sector.
